finding.what: The behaviour key calls two mechanisms equal when they behave differently. effective() sets to 0.0 every constant that no live score or pick instruction reads. The learning principle, however, works on the whole theta vector: it starts from all of it (Acquirer.__init__ A[0]=start) and can mix coordinates with the cross-dimension ops 'mean' and 'norm' (design_o.py 515-519), which are in A_UNARY and can be inserted by edits into init, propose or update. The values of unread constants therefore change the step sizes and population of the dimensions that are read.
finding.why_it_matters: discovery.py keys its memo of (score, cpu) and its 'seen' set by this key. A candidate that differs from its parent only in an unread constant, for example after a 'perturb' or a 'grow' into a dead register, is either dropped as 'seen' or handed the measured value of a different mechanism. At acceptance, measure(mechanism, 'accepted') can return the score of another mechanism. The ledger runs themselves are keyed by the full digest and are correct, so the discovery decisions and the values the recursive learner learns from disagree with what the accepted mechanism actually does.
finding.evidence: check2.py: g1 = default + theta[10]=5.0 + init [ones 1; mean 2 0; abs 2 2; mul 1 1 2]; g2 identical except theta[10]=90.0. edits.behaviour(g1)==edits.behaviour(g2) -> True. Acquirer step sizes are 0.4545 vs 7.2727. With seed 7 the learned theta[:3] is [-1.65,-5.55,-3.58] vs [-12.97,-10.97,-16.61], and the answers on fresh problems differ (seeds 7 and 8).
finding.suggested_fix: Keep the real values of all constants in the key, and drop only dead score and pick instructions. Alternatively, zero unread constants only when init, propose and update contain no cross-coordinate op (mean, norm).

verdict.evidence:
I ran WORK/behaviour_mix_check.py (behav_mix.py in WORK), an Acquirer-only check that takes seconds. It builds two mechanisms from default(), each with an 11th unread constant, set to 0.0 in one and 40.0 in the other, and compares their first proposals with the same rng seed.
- init [ones 1; scale 1 1 9] (no cross-coordinate op): behaviour equal True, digest equal False, proposals on dims 0..9 identical True (maxdiff 0.0).
- init [... mean 2 0 0; add 1 1 2]: behaviour equal True, digest equal False, proposals on dims 0..9 identical False (maxdiff 9.86).
- init [norm 0 0 0; ones 1 0 0]: behaviour equal True, digest equal False, proposals on dims 0..9 identical False (maxdiff 2.44).
Code paths:
- edits.py:194-195 builds the 'used' set from score and pick only.
- discovery.py:111-115 returns the memo value without running when the key matches.
- run_dev.py:63-66 shares one memo across lineages.
verdict.better_fix: In effective(), zero the unread constants only when no instruction in init, propose or update uses 'mean' or 'norm'; otherwise keep every theta value. This keeps the deduplication benefit in the common case and stays sound. The simplest alternative is to keep the full theta in the key and drop only dead score and pick instructions. Also add a regression test that perturbs an unread constant under a 'mean' init and asserts the keys differ. If more cross-coordinate A-ops are added later, put them in a named tuple (e.g. A_MIXING) and test membership in it, rather than hard-coding the two names.

finding.what: Generation 0 of design o is not the first design's prior and cross-entropy search in another machine. (a) shortlist is 1, while design a's default (version.py) is 4. Each construction of design a therefore costs about 4 times the units on free problems, which gives design a about 4 times fewer cross-entropy rounds from the same training budget, a different construction at test time (design a's shortlist is halved to 2 by the test meter) and a different leftover budget for _improve. (b) The search space is 10 constants over relation 0 and attribute 0 only. There is no per-group, rem, oa, occ (next/left) or optsum term and no var2 feature; on jobshop, whose only relation data is occ_attr, design o gen0 can learn nothing from relations. (c) The sigma floor is 0.1 against 0.02. (d) The held-back check chooses among 3 vectors (start, mean, last_best) against 2 in design a. (e) The dhard term is mm(dhard) where design a uses amount/top, which keeps zero, so the prior differs whenever every allowed option already has a violation. The docstring says the test-time answer is chosen 'so that what differs between designs is what acquisition produced'; that is false, because the untrained answers already differ.
finding.why_it_matters: Any comparison of the two designs at generation 0 ('against generation 0 of both designs' in evaluate.py) mixes the machine with the shortlist, the iteration count, the test-time improvement budget, CPU and the representation. A gain of design o over design a could come from 3 to 4 times more cross-entropy rounds per unit rather than from the open design.
finding.evidence: smoke.log: design a 'iters 2' on pmedian, knapsack, partitioning and setcover; design o 'iters 8/7/6/6'. knapsack untrained is 0.8510 for a and 0.8515 for o, so the answers differ before any acquisition. pmedian CPU is 3.0s for a and 8.5s for o. version.py: 'shortlist': ('choice',(1,2,4,8),4). learner.py 501: sigma floor 0.02; design_o.py 109: floor CONST[5]=0.1.
finding.suggested_fix: State these differences in the docstring and in the registration. For a design comparison, either set design o gen0's shortlist to 4 with a 0.02 floor and a 2-way check, or compare designs only at matched units and CPU with the shortlist reported. Do not describe generation 0 of design o as 'the first design in this machine'.

verdict.reasoning: I checked each sub-claim against the code, and all five hold. (a) design_o.default() sets "shortlist": 1 (design_o.py:111), while version.py:37 sets the design a default to 4. Both designs' _cost multiplies by the shortlist on free problems (learner.py:427-428, design_o.py:661-662), so design a pays about 4 times as much per rollout. smoke.log shows the result: 'iters 2' for a against 6-8 for o. (b) The gen0 score program reads only dsoft, dhard, used, prev[0], vo[0] and neigh[0], plus a step on dhard. The pick program reads vvdone[0], vvopen[0] and vattr[0]. There are 10 thetas. Design a by default turns on per_group, rem, opt_attr, occ (next and left) and optsum (version.py:25-33), and it adds var2 features when the shortlist is above 1 (learner.py:310-313). Design o gen0 never reads occnext. (c) The update floor is CONST[5]=0.1 (design_o.py:109) against 0.02 (learner.py:501). (d) SELECT 'best_of_3' compares start, state and last_best (design_o.py:718-724). Design a compares [start, best_theta] (learner.py:530). (e) Design o applies 'mm' to the raw dhard: (x-lo)/(hi-lo) at design_o.py:226-228. Design a uses amount/top (learner.py:212-215). So when every allowed option has a violation, the smallest one maps to 0 in design o and to a positive value in design a. The untrained knapsack numbers in smoke.log also differ (0.8510 against 0.8515). The module docstring says the test-time answer makes 'what differs between designs is what acquisition produced', and default() calls gen0 'the first design's prior, in this machine'. Neither statement is accurate. How much this matters is limited. evaluate.py uses a0 only as a reference baseline (line 103). The compute-matched control is built on o0 (line 122), and claims (1)-(3) compare discovered mechanisms with o0 and its matched control, not o0 with a0. So the defect does not invalidate the primary claims. It does invalidate any reading of o0 against a0 as an effect of 'the machine' or 'the open design', and it misdescribes the baseline. I rate it minor: a documentation and interpretation problem, not one that breaks the main comparisons.
verdict.evidence: design_o.py:111 '"shortlist": 1'; version.py:37 '"shortlist": ("choice", (1, 2, 4, 8), 4)'; learner.py:427-428 and design_o.py:661-662 'factor = shortlist if not P.ordered else 1'; design_o.py:109 '["floor", 1, 1, 5]' with CONST[5]=0.1 against learner.py:501 'np.maximum(sigma * v["model.decay"], 0.02)'; design_o.py:718-724 three-way choice against learner.py:530 'np.stack([start, best_theta])'; design_o.py:382-383 raw dhard plus 'mm' at 226-228 against learner.py:212-215 'amount / top'; version.py:25-33 feat.per_group/rem/opt_attr/occ/optsum default 1; the gen0 score program (design_o.py:92-98) uses sensor indices 0, 1, 3, 5, 6, 8 only, never occnext (12); smoke.log lines 4-11 show 'iters 2' for a against 8/7/6/6 for o, and untrained knapsack 0.8510 against 0.8515; evaluate.py:103,122 has a0 as a reference baseline, with the matched control built on o0.
verdict.better_fix: Fix the docstrings of the module and of default() first. State that o0 is a reduced linear prior and that o0's acquisition differs from a0's in shortlist, sigma floor, held-back selection and dhard scaling. If a0 against o0 or discovered-mechanism against a0 is to be reported as a design effect, also add an 'a0-matched' variant of o0 for evaluate.py: shortlist 4, floor 0.02, a 2-way check, amount/top scaling for dhard, and occnext/optsum/rem terms. Alternatively, report a0 only with a compute-matched control built from a0 itself, so that any gain over a0 is not read as an effect of the machine.
